ei.title: Practice 03 — 인터넷의 정보를 평가할 수 있는 비판적 사고능력의 중요성
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본2

fullPassage: The upside of the Internet is that it is democratic ― anyone can say what they like ― but the downside is that there is no quality control. Far from being an electronic oracle infallibly dispensing wisdom, it contains the views not only of credentialed experts but also of uninformed idiots ― and everything in between. There is, of course, a huge amount of useful, accurate and trustworthy information online, but it is not always easy to find. Search engines like Google may help, but it is important to keep in mind that page rankings are determined by popularity rather than truth. Since conspiracy theories surrounding events such as 9/11 are popular, they are likely to appear high on such rankings, but this does not mean they are true. So if we are to avoid being misled, we need not only the ability to locate information, but also the critical thinking skills to evaluate it.

questions.passage: The upside of the Internet is that it is ①<u>democratic</u> ― anyone can say what they like ― but the downside is that there is no quality control. Far from being an electronic oracle infallibly ②<u>dispense</u> wisdom, it contains the views not only of credentialed experts but also of uninformed idiots ― and everything in between. There is, of course, a huge amount of useful, accurate and trustworthy information online, but it is not always easy to find. Search engines like Google may help, but it is important to keep in mind that page rankings are ③<u>determined</u> by popularity rather than truth. Since conspiracy theories ④<u>surrounding</u> events such as 9/11 are popular, they are likely to appear high on such rankings, but this does not mean they are true. So if we are to avoid being misled, we need not only the ability to locate information, but also the critical thinking skills to evaluate it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① democratic=민주적인(형용사 보어 정상), ② dispensing→dispense 오류(oracle을 후치수식하는 현재분사 dispensing이 맞음. dispense 원형은 분사 역할 불가), ③ determined=결정된(수동 과거분사 정상), ④ surrounding=둘러싸는(현재분사 후치수식 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① democratic: 'it is democratic' — 형용사 보어 정상
✅ ② dispense: 'an electronic oracle infallibly dispensing wisdom'에서 oracle을 후치수식하는 현재분사 dispensing이 맞음. dispense(원형)로 쓰면 분사 역할 불가 → ②가 틀린 것
❌ ③ determined: 'page rankings are determined by popularity' — be+p.p. 수동태 정상
❌ ④ surrounding: 'events surrounding events such as 9/11' — 현재분사 후치수식 정상
det.tip: 명사 후치수식 현재분사: 능동 의미 → -ing. 'an oracle dispensing wisdom' = 지혜를 나눠주는 신탁. 원형(dispense)으로 쓰면 분사구문 불가

questions.passage: The upside of the Internet is that it is democratic ― anyone can say what they like ― but the downside is that there is no quality control. Far from being an electronic oracle ①<u>infallibly</u> dispensing wisdom, it contains the views not only of credentialed experts but also of uninformed idiots ― and everything in between. There is, of course, a huge amount of useful, accurate and ②<u>trustworthy</u> information online, but it is not always easy to find. Search engines like Google may help, but it is important ③<u>keeping</u> in mind that page rankings are determined by popularity rather than truth. Since conspiracy theories surrounding events such as 9/11 are popular, they are likely to appear high on such rankings, but this does not mean they are true. So if we are to avoid being ④<u>misled</u>, we need not only the ability to locate information, but also the critical thinking skills to evaluate it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① infallibly=절대적으로(부사 수식 정상), ② trustworthy=믿을 수 있는(형용사 나열 정상), ③ keeping→to keep 오류(가주어-진주어 구문에서 to부정사가 맞음), ④ misled=오도된(수동 과거분사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① infallibly: 'infallibly dispensing' — 부사 수식 정상
❌ ② trustworthy: 'useful, accurate and trustworthy information' — 형용사 나열 정상
✅ ③ keeping: 'it is important to keep in mind'에서 가주어 it / 진주어 to부정사 구문. to keep이 맞음. keeping으로 쓰면 비문 → ③이 틀린 것
❌ ④ misled: 'avoid being misled' — 수동 과거분사 정상
det.tip: 가주어 it + is + 형용사 + to부정사: 'It is important to V'. keeping으로 쓰면 진주어 자리에 동명사가 오는 형태가 되어 가주어 it과 이중 주어 충돌

questions.passage: The upside of the Internet is ①<u>what it is democratic</u> ― anyone can say what they like ― but the downside is that there is no quality control. Far from being an electronic oracle infallibly dispensing wisdom, it contains the views not only of ②<u>credentialed</u> experts but also of uninformed idiots ― and everything in between. There is, of course, a huge amount of useful, accurate and trustworthy information online, but it is not always easy to find. Search engines like Google may help, but it is important to keep in mind that page rankings are determined by popularity rather than truth. Since conspiracy theories surrounding events such as 9/11 are popular, they are ③<u>likely</u> to appear high on such rankings, but this does not mean they are true. So if we are to avoid being misled, we need not only the ability to locate information, but also the critical thinking skills ④<u>to evaluate</u> it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① what→that 오류(명사절 접속사 자리. 'The upside is that...'에서 that이 맞음. what으로 쓰면 선행사 없는 관계사로 비문), ② credentialed=자격 있는(형용사 정상), ③ likely=~할 것 같은(형용사 정상), ④ to evaluate=평가하기 위해(형용사적 to부정사 정상)
det.analysis:
✅ ① what it is democratic: 'The upside of the Internet is that it is democratic'에서 that은 보어 명사절 접속사. what으로 쓰면 선행사 없는 관계사가 되어 'The upside is what it is democratic'이 되는데 it이 이미 주어이므로 비문 → ①이 틀린 것
❌ ② credentialed: 'credentialed experts' — 형용사 수식 정상
❌ ③ likely: 'they are likely to appear high' — be likely to 정상
❌ ④ to evaluate: 'skills to evaluate it' — 형용사적 to부정사(명사 수식) 정상
det.tip: 명사절 접속사 that vs 관계대명사 what: 'S is that + 완전한 절' → that. 'S is what + 불완전한 절' → what. 'it is democratic'은 완전한 절이므로 that

questions.passage: The upside of the Internet is that it is ①<u>democratic</u> ― anyone can say what they like ― but the downside is that there is no quality control. Far from being an electronic oracle infallibly dispensing wisdom, it contains the views not only of credentialed experts but also of uninformed idiots ― and everything in between. There is, of course, a huge amount of useful, accurate and ②<u>trustworthy</u> information online, but it is not always easy to find. Search engines like Google may help, but it is important to keep in mind that page rankings are determined by ③<u>popularity</u> rather than truth. Since conspiracy theories surrounding events such as 9/11 are popular, they are likely to appear high on such rankings, but this does not mean they are true. So if we are to ④<u>accept</u> being misled, we need not only the ability to locate information, but also the critical thinking skills to evaluate it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① democratic=민주적인(누구나 말할 수 있다 — 적절), ② trustworthy=믿을 수 있는(신뢰할 수 있는 정보 — 적절), ③ popularity=인기도(페이지 순위 기준 — 적절), ④ accept→avoid가 맞음(오도되는 것을 '받아들이면' 안 되고 '피해야' 함)
det.analysis:
❌ ① democratic: '인터넷은 민주적' — 도입부 문맥에 적절
❌ ② trustworthy: '유용하고 정확하고 신뢰할 수 있는 정보' — 적절
❌ ③ popularity: '페이지 순위는 인기도에 의해 결정' — 적절
✅ ④ accept: 'if we are to avoid being misled'에서 오도되는 것을 '받아들이다(accept)'가 아니라 '피하다(avoid)'가 맞음. accept는 문맥상 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: avoid = 피하다. accept = 받아들이다. 오도(mislead)를 '피하려면(avoid)' 비판적 사고가 필요하다는 글의 핵심 논리

questions.passage: The upside of the Internet is that it is democratic ― anyone can say what they like ― but the downside is that there is no ①<u>quality control</u>. Far from being an electronic oracle infallibly dispensing wisdom, it contains the views not only of credentialed experts but also of ②<u>well-informed</u> idiots ― and everything in between. There is, of course, a huge amount of useful, ③<u>accurate</u> and trustworthy information online, but it is not always easy to find. Search engines like Google may help, but it is important to keep in mind that page rankings are determined by popularity rather than truth. Since conspiracy theories surrounding events such as 9/11 are popular, they are likely to appear high on such rankings, but this does not mean they are true. So if we are to avoid being misled, we need not only the ability to locate information, but also the ④<u>critical</u> thinking skills to evaluate it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① quality control=품질 관리(없다는 단점 — 적절), ② well-informed→uninformed가 맞음(정보에 어두운 바보들 — well-informed는 잘 아는 사람, 문맥상 credentialed experts와 대조 파괴), ③ accurate=정확한(적절), ④ critical=비판적인(적절)
det.analysis:
❌ ① quality control: '품질 관리가 없다' — 인터넷 단점으로 적절
✅ ② well-informed: 'not only of credentialed experts but also of uninformed idiots'에서 credentialed experts(자격 있는 전문가)와 대조되는 표현이 uninformed idiots(정보에 어두운 바보들). well-informed(잘 아는)로 바꾸면 대조 구조가 무너져 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ accurate: '유용하고 정확한 정보' — 적절
❌ ④ critical: '비판적 사고 능력' — 글의 핵심어로 적절
det.tip: credentialed experts(자격 있는 전문가) vs uninformed idiots(무지한 바보) — not only A but also B 대조 구조. well-informed로 쓰면 양쪽이 모두 긍정적이 되어 대비 消失

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: popularity=인기도 (페이지 순위는 진실이 아닌 인기도에 의해 결정됨)
det.analysis: 빈칸 위치: 'page rankings are determined by _____ rather than truth.' 뒤 문장에서 음모론이 인기 있어서 높은 순위에 나타난다고 했으므로 순위 기준 = 인기도(popularity). truth(진실)는 rather than 뒤에 있으므로 빈칸 답이 될 수 없음. wisdom/quality는 문맥 무관
det.tip: rather than truth = 진실이 아닌. 빈칸은 '진실이 아닌 어떤 기준'이어야 하고, 뒤 문장이 단서(음모론 인기 → 높은 순위)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: locate information=정보를 찾는 능력 (not only A but also B에서 A 자리)
det.analysis: 빈칸: 'we need not only the ability to _____, but also the critical thinking skills to evaluate it.' B = 비판적으로 평가하는 능력(evaluate it). A는 단순히 정보를 찾는(locate information) 능력. evaluate it은 이미 B에 나오므로 A에 사용 불가. trust experts/use search engines는 글 전체 맥락과 무관
det.tip: not only A but also B: A = 찾는 능력(locate), B = 평가하는 능력(evaluate). 두 능력을 대비시키는 구조

questions.passage: The upside of the Internet is that it is democratic ― anyone can say what they like ― but the downside is that there is no quality control. Far from being <u>an electronic oracle infallibly dispensing wisdom</u>, it contains the views not only of credentialed experts but also of uninformed idiots ― and everything in between. There is, of course, a huge amount of useful, accurate and trustworthy information online, but it is not always easy to find. Search engines like Google may help, but it is important to keep in mind that page rankings are determined by popularity rather than truth. Since conspiracy theories surrounding events such as 9/11 are popular, they are likely to appear high on such rankings, but this does not mean they are true. So if we are to avoid being misled, we need not only the ability to locate information, but also the critical thinking skills to evaluate it.

밑줄 표현: 'Far from being an electronic oracle infallibly dispensing wisdom' — 역접 'Far from'으로 시작하므로 인터넷은 이런 존재가 아님을 강조. oracle = 신탁(절대적 진리를 말하는 존재), infallibly = 절대 틀리지 않게, dispensing wisdom = 지혜를 나눠줌
✅ ①: '오류 없이 지혜를 전달하는 완전무결한 정보 제공자' — oracle+infallibly+dispensing wisdom의 직접적 의미를 정확히 반영
❌ ②: 민주적 수용은 글의 도입부 내용
❌ ③: 검증된 지식 저장소도 oracle의 함축과 다름
❌ ④: 토론 공간은 oracle의 함축과 무관
